question.problem:
$$
X=[\begin{aligned}7 & 6 & 8 \\ -1 & -3 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the observation matrix $X$ above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the mean-deviation form of $X.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the mean-deviation form of the observation matrix

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}| & | &  & | \\ {x}_{1} & {x}_{2} & ⋯ & {x}_{n} \\ | & | &  & |\end{aligned}]
$$

is given by 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}| & | &  & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & ⋯ & {b}_{n} \\ | & | &  & |\end{aligned}]
$$

where ${b}_{i}={x}_{i}-m$ for $i=1,2,…,n,$ and $m$ is sample mean vector.

From the matrix, we have that  

$$
{x}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

As a result, the sample mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{1}{3}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}([\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}21 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={x}_{1}-m=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{2} & ={x}_{2}-m=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{3} & ={x}_{3}-m=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the mean-deviation form is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
